function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Here’s a quick guide to help you find a place where you can order a cake—whether it’s for a birthday, wedding, or just a sweet treat. | Category | What to Look For | Typical Options | |----------|------------------|-----------------| | **Local Bakeries** | • Freshness & quality
• Personal touch & custom designs
• Support your community | • Your neighborhood bakery (e.g., “Sweet Treats Bakery” on Main St.)
• Specialty shops that offer custom cakes (e.g., “The Cake Studio” in your city) | | **Online Delivery Platforms** | • Wide selection from multiple bakers
• Easy ordering & payment
• Delivery tracking | • **Goldbelly** – delivers specialty cakes nationwide (great for unique flavors)
• **Bakeology** – offers a curated list of artisan bakeries with delivery
• **Etsy** – many independent bakers sell custom cakes here | | **National Chains** | • Consistency & reliability
• Quick turnaround | • **Panera Bread** – offers custom cakes for birthdays
• **Dunkin’ Donuts** – has a “Cake Delivery” option in many locations
• **Baker’s Dozen** – a chain that specializes in custom cakes | | **Specialty Dessert Shops** | • Unique flavor profiles
• Artistic presentation | • **Milk Bar** – known for creative desserts (check their website for delivery)
• **Magnolia Bakery** – famous for cupcakes and cakes (delivery via third‑party apps) | | **Third‑Party Food Delivery Apps** | • Convenience & speed
• Real‑time updates | • **Uber Eats**, **DoorDash**, **Grubhub** – many local bakeries partner with these apps for instant delivery | ### How to Choose the Right Option 1. **Check Reviews** - Look at Google, Yelp, or TripAdvisor ratings. - Read recent customer photos to gauge freshness and presentation. 2. **Confirm Delivery Area** - Some local shops only deliver within a 10‑15 mile radius. - National platforms often ship across state lines but may charge extra. 3. **Ask About Customization** - If you want a specific design, theme, or dietary restriction (gluten‑free, vegan), confirm the baker can accommodate. 4. **Know the Cut‑Off Times** - Most bakeries require orders 24–48 hours in advance for special occasions. - Online platforms usually have a “next‑day” or “same‑day” delivery window. 5. **Compare Prices** - Factor in delivery fees, tip, and any packaging costs. - Some sites offer free delivery over a certain amount. ### Quick Order Checklist - **Occasion**: Birthday, anniversary, corporate event, etc. - **Size & Shape**: Round, square, tiered, mini cupcakes. - **Flavor & Frosting**: Classic vanilla, chocolate, lemon, or something exotic. - **Decoration**: Plain, fondant, edible images, custom toppers. - **Dietary Needs**: Gluten‑free, dairy‑free, nut‑free, vegan. - **Delivery Date & Time**: Confirm the exact slot. --- #### Example Order Flow (Using an Online Platform) 1. **Visit the site** (e.g., Goldbelly). 2. **Search** for “birthday cake” + your city. 3. **Filter** by price, rating, or dietary preference. 4. **Select** a cake, add to cart, and proceed to checkout. 5. **Enter** delivery address, choose a time slot, and pay securely. 6. **Track** the order via the platform’s app or email notifications. --- If you let me know your city or zip code, I can suggest a few specific bakeries or online services that operate in your area. Happy cake hunting!
